The hotel environment is dark. When checking in, the staff recommended paying extra to upgrade to a suite. The room was very large, and the cabinet door was poorly designed. We had a very pleasant stay at this hotel and found many things to love. The location is excellent—just a short walk to metro stations and bus stops, and about 15 minutes on foot to Ximending. It’s close enough to the action but still quiet at night, which was perfect for us. There are also several kid-friendly attractions nearby, which made getting around with our son easy and enjoyable.
The hotel offers a free shuttle service, which is a great convenience, although it would be even better if it started earlier and ran more frequently. One of the highlights of our stay was the free guided tour—our guide was amazing! She spoke fluent English, was very knowledgeable, and made the experience truly memorable.
Another charming feature is the old-school snack corner, which is complimentary for guests. It’s a nostalgic and fun touch. It’s not available 24/7 (unlike another hotel we stayed at in Taiwan), but since it’s part of the restaurant area, it follows their opening hours—which is understandable.
The staff deserve special praise—they were consistently helpful, proactive, and kind. From check-in to daily interactions, everyone made us feel welcome and well taken care of.
The rooms have recently been renovated and look fresh and modern. I particularly appreciated the switch from carpeted to hard floors—it feels much cleaner and more hygienic. The room itself is spacious, with ample closet space, and the layout is thoughtful, especially for families.
However, the bathroom design could use some improvement. While I liked the concept of having a bathtub in the shower area—great for kids to enjoy a bath without splashing everywhere—the tub design wasn't very family-friendly. It's a Japanese-style, tiled tub with sharp edges, and I got scratched multiple times. It doesn’t feel safe for young children. The wooden rack and bucket also had visible mold, and mold was beginning to appear around the tub edges as well. This was disappointing, especially since my son has sensitive skin and developed a rash after using the tub.
Despite the bathroom concerns, we still had a great overall experience. I would recommend this hotel for its convenient location, friendly staff, thoughtful services, and family-friendly features—just be cautious about the tub if you're traveling with young children or anyone with sensitive skin.

First time for us in Taipei so we decided location near the Main mrt station was top priority. It is a little over our normal budget but worth every cent. Breakfast is decent and I wish it was open a little earlier than 7 am. We got free coffee vouchers at their cafe and was delish. The last day rained like crazy but we didn’t get wet going back to the airport, exactly because of the location.  It’s a tiny bit in need for some renovations and i hit my head with the low ceiling while taking a shower but otherwise ok.

I am writing this at 2.30am. 

Booked a triple room with 3 single beds from 1-2 
Dec 23. Checked in close to 10pm. The front desk was friendly and super impressive! Helped sorted out problem with my phone data card. :)

We returned to the room close to midnight after dinner Had problem with turning on hand shower. No big deal as rain shower was working. Rubber mat in bath tub was pretty useless. I almost slipped and fell when I went into the bathtub.

In the middle of my bathe, the light suddenly went off. There was a power trip. But that occured after a family member plugged in hair dryer. Had to quickly call front desk to fix. Was told they can fixed the fused bulb in a couple of minutes. The electrician came quickly but took 30 mins to fix the problem.  

When I got onto my bed and turned the pillow, got  a rude shock! Saw a cockroach of about 2cm in between the 2 pillows! Too stunned to take pic before the cockroach ran away. I called front desk to request for change of room but was told the hotel is full tonight. 

Help came quickly and caught the cockroach in abt 10mins from the time of my call. 

What an eventful night. 
Had to sleep on the same  bed knowing there could be more pests lurking somewhere. Pray all be ok for rest of night. So glad my stay is only 1 night. 

Never ever gonna come back here again, will definitely pay a lot more to stay in the usual chain of hotels and put up with less ideal location.

What a way to start my vacation.

But we probably won’t stay in this hotel again due to the reaction of the manager on duty ( she has foreign accent while she speaks mandarin).

In addition, we received emergency drill notifications once a week during our stay, quite disturbing.

The lighting environment of the hotel is very dim. There is no door to the bathroom and only a curtain. It feels like there is no privacy because I have a child, and he is a boy! not feeling well! Also, the bathtub is designed to be relatively high, and I almost fell when I stepped out of it. This is a hidden danger for the elderly and children! The facilities in the room are relatively advanced but not suitable for older people who are not very good at using them! Also, when we arrived at the room in the middle of the night, we discovered that the hotel did not provide disposable items, so we called the front desk. Fortunately, they were willing to give us a toothbrush🪥 and toothpaste, otherwise we would have to go out to buy them in the middle of the night! I also asked the front desk if there was a shower cap, otherwise I would get wet after taking a shower. The gentleman at the front desk spoke in a very strange tone, which could be heard on the phone. I think I have always stayed in five-star hotels, and these disposable items are originally spare parts and will be provided to everyone. of the guest room! Later, the shower cap was still not delivered to me! Although the hotel claims to be environmentally friendly and green, it must also provide guest convenience first because the price of a five-star hotel is not cheap in Taipei, and check-out has to be at 11 o'clock. I just checked in early in the morning! In the next two days, we also stayed at the Taipei Grand Hyatt Hotel and the Banqiao Hilton Hotel. These two hotels did not have these problems. The check-in was very good, the disposable supplies were all complete, and we checked out after twelve o'clock. The service was very good!

shortcoming. The hotel facilities are a bit old. When we were sleeping soundly, the mirror in the bathroom suddenly fell down and the whole family was woken up by the noise. Called housekeeping early in the morning. Arrange for repairs.
advantage. The location is convenient and the breakfast is satisfactory.

The Q Square Mall is next door, making it easy to grab whatever you need for the trip. The room was clean, the breakfast was okay, and the staff were generally nice. I also requested for a baby cot / baby bottle heater and was duly provided with that. I am satisfied with the additional items. Location wise, it is next to a shopping mall which I can get food easily either at basement 3 or 5th floor. The underground levels of the mall are also connected to the train transit system. The ground floor is connected to the bus terminal. I think this is a plus point. I did request for a late checkout and the hotel accommodated. I reckon this was due to the above incident. Ground level lobby staff were friendly and nice.

Super conveniently located, directly above Taipei Main Station which gives great access to the Tamsui-Xinyi Line, as well as the Bannan Line. There was also the vast Taipei Underground mall that leads to many locations, like Shin Kong Mitsukoshi Taipei Station, and Breeze Taipei Station, so one is never bored and there are places to go even in inclement weather.

As for the hotel itself, let's just say it DEFINITELY has its charms. The décor is quaint and aged, and the room definitely is showing it's age, but the aesthetic was not necessarily a negative. It's just a certain kind of charm that takes awhile 2 appreciate.

Age and décor aside, the hotel totally makes it up with it's service. The staff were very attentive, efficient and friendly. From the front desk, concierge, down to the wait staff at the breakfast restaurant, we were treated very warmly.

As for the negative, the air-conditioning is actually central and when we checked in, our room aircon was not cold and was rather warm, turns out that the filter was very dirty and not well-maintained, but kudos to the maintenance staff who was quick and efficient in trying to rectify the issue. Throughout our stay though, the aircon still had its ups and downs, but that is what was to be expected from a central aircon system I guess.

Overall, very much recommended for its location and service.

My father and I arrived late at night at about 11pm, and the front desk got us into our room very quickly. We quickly showered and fell asleep after marveling at the locations of the light switches and that there were master switches by the beds so that you didn't have to get up again.

We purchased breakfast at the hotel each day we were there, and they have an excellent spread for breakfast. About 8 hot items, some of which rotate, but they include: Steamed Veggies, meatball with shark fin and roe sauce, chef special chicken, tempura fried burdock, chicken sausage and bacon, congee, oden soup, and alternating siu mai and custard buns. Then they have a made to order area where you can get eggs in any style, or choose one of three different types of noodles. All soups that came from this kitchen morning or night were excellent. Then they have a refrigerated section with fresh fruit and yogurts. This was followed by a large salad bar, which included more cold entrees. Finally, against the other wall were make your own noodle bowl area, a few fried things, and breads.

The only knock on this entire hotel was the coffee bar, where we did see two bugs running around, one under the machines and one on the wall behind them.

The sauna is a wonderful place to relax, and the gym is well equipped and opens at 6 each morning so that you can start your day off right and breakfast starts at 6:30.

Location is excellent, it's right off of the freeway, and you walk 2 blocks around the technical university and you're at the MRT.

All of the staff were incredibly accommodating, and I plan to stay at this hotel during future visits to Taipei.

However, the taste was a bit peculiar, and the orange juice, for example, was low in juice, which was disappointing. The distance from Ximen Station, about 13 minutes, was a bit far. The sheets, towels, and bottled water were changed daily, making it comfortable, and the staff at the front desk and breakfast area were friendly. Although the hotel is old, I think it's reasonably priced.
Very nice hotel. Although it's old it is well maintained and the room was very big. Stains on the sheets, pillowcase and carpet but for such an old hotel it's understandable.

Humble House was well-located for the purposes of our trip. The staff was attentive and helpful. The room was kept clean. We just needed to request for extra towels and toilet paper the first day because only one set for one pax was provided.
Although it is an old hotel, the location is good, next to the MRT station

Very nice hotel. Excellent service & good food served. Thanks for making my stay a comfortable one

Since I stayed in Taichung before heading to Taipei, I decided to stay at this Japanese hotel. It was an exceptional hotel in every aspect, making it difficult to find any negative points.  
【Location】It takes only a few minutes to arrive from MRT Nanjing Fuxing Station. There are various convenience stores and shops nearby, and access from the station is easy, so the location is quite good, and I didn't find it inconvenient. However, I had to transfer at Zhongshan Station from Taipei Station, and since I came to Taipei Station by high-speed rail, I had to carry a lot of luggage to MRT Taipei Station. Because I had a lot of bags and found this somewhat troublesome, I decided to take a taxi from Taipei Station to the hotel, but taxis are generally inexpensive in Taiwan, so I was glad I used one. My recommendation is to use the MRT Airport Line between Taoyuan Airport and Taipei, and then take a taxi from MRT Taipei to the hotel. There was even a place within walking distance where I could enjoy breakfast from 5:30 AM, so I enjoyed the night market via MRT and local breakfast options.  
【Hotel】Upon entering the entrance, I was immediately guided to the reception, where a staff member, who was Taiwanese, assisted me in Japanese, so I had no troubles at all. The lobby is likely a high-ceilinged open space, resembling a square tube in image, and I was charmed by a pleasant fragrance that I found appealing. The cleaning of the guest rooms was perfect. By the way, when using a taxi from the hotel, the hotel staff informs the driver of the destination, which was very helpful.  
【Bedding】There were both bathrobes and sleepwear provided.  
【Toilet】By the way, like in many places in Taiwan, toilet paper cannot be flushed; there is a foot-operated trash can close to the toilet where you are expected to dispose of your waste. I was initially confused, but I got used to it quickly.  
【Hotel Meals】I also arranged breakfast, and it was indeed a high-ranking buffet with a variety of ingredients that caught my eye. Everything was delicious, and I wished I had room in my stomach for more. By the way, there were quite a few Japanese guests as well.  
【Others】There was a gym and a pool, but I couldn't use them due to sightseeing time; I hope to take advantage of them next time.
The place to stay is good and the staff is friendly. You can visit again~

The rooms are quite spacious, despite being weirdly designed. The location is also inconvenient and is not close to public transport or any tourist attractions. Food is difficult to find nearby, and the neighbourhood feels quite dead in general.
However, the staff where extremely helpful when I fell ill, and helped me book an appointment at a clinic and arranged transportation - their care and support was the best I ever encountered, and I am forever grateful.
